pass_b_english: And if “every evil word is an abomination to the Lord your God”, how great an abomination must we think the evil word of denial to be, and the evil speech that proclaims another god, and the evil oath by the fortune of men, a thing without substance? When this oath is put to us, we must remember the one who taught, “But I say to you, do not swear at all” (Matthew 5:34). For if the one who swears by heaven offends against the throne of God, and the one who swears by the earth commits impiety, making a god of what is called the footstool of God's feet, and the one who swears by Jerusalem sins, even though it is the city of the great King, and the one who swears by his own head does wrong (Matthew 5:34-36), how great a sin must we think it to swear by someone's fortune? At that time we must also remember the saying, “Of every idle word you will give an account on the day of judgment” (Matthew 12:36). For what other word is as idle as the oath sworn in denial?

But it is likely that the enemy will want to outwit us, by whatever means he can, into bowing down “to the sun or the moon or all the array of heaven”. But we will say that the Word of God “did not command” these things (Deuteronomy 17:3). For we must in no way bow down to created things when the Creator is present, who suffices for all and comes in time to the prayer of all. Not even the sun himself would wish to be bowed down to by those of God's portion, and probably not by anyone else either. Rather, imitating the one who said, “Why do you call me good? No one is good but one, God the Father” (Mark 10:18), he would say, as it were, to the one who wishes to bow down to him:

“Why do you call me god? There is one true God. And why do you bow down to me? ‘For you shall bow down to the Lord your God and serve him alone’ (Matthew 4:10). I too am a created being. Why do you want to bow down to one who himself bows down? For I too bow down to God the Father and serve him, and in obedience to his commands I have been subjected to futility because of him who subjected it in hope, and I shall be set free from the bondage of corruption, though I too am now bound to a perishable body, into the freedom of the glory of the children of God (Romans 8:20-21).”
